decisions.choice: four women: his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene
alternatives: three women: his mother's sister is Mary the wife of Clopas
two women: his mother and her sister, named as the two Marys
decisions.reason: The Greek has no "and" between "his mother's sister" and "Mary of Clopas", so they could be the same woman. But then two sisters would both be called Mary, which is unlikely. Read as four, the list falls into two pairs joined by "and": two women not named, then two named Marys. The evidence is not decisive.

decisions.choice: Mary the wife of Clopas
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "Mary of Clopas", a way of naming a woman by a man she belonged to, most often her husband, sometimes her father or son. "Wife" is the usual sense. Nothing more is known of Clopas; whether he is the Cleopas of Luke 24:18 is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Magdalene: from Magdala, a town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Mary Magdalene is named here for the first time in John; she is the first to find the tomb empty and to see the risen Jesus (20:1-18). Luke 8:2 says Jesus had freed her from seven demons.

decisions.choice: his mother's sister: John does not name her
decisions.reason: Other Gospels name women at the cross: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and Salome or the mother of Zebedee's sons (Matthew 27:56; Mark 15:40). Whether John's unnamed sister of Jesus's mother is one of these cannot be known from the text.

decisions.choice: Meanwhile (B); Some women were standing (R)
decisions.reason: The sentence turns from the soldiers to the people who loved Jesus (19:24 meaning decision m1). Balanced marks the turn with "Meanwhile"; Readable starts with the women and then lists them, without saying how many (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: María la de Cleofás (L); María la esposa de Cleofás (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Cleofás" is the form Spanish has long used for this name; it does not settle whether he is the Cleopas of Luke 24:18 (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "la de", the Spanish way of naming a woman by her husband or family, which matches the Greek; Balanced and Readable say "esposa", the usual sense.

decisions.choice: Mientras tanto (B); Cerca de la cruz de Jesús había unas mujeres (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the sentence turns from the soldiers to the people who loved Jesus (19:24, meaning decision m1). Readable names the women after saying they were there, without saying how many (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Marie de Magdala
decisions.reason: "Marie-Madeleine" is the traditional French name, but it hides what the Greek word says, that she came from Magdala (meaning decision m3); "Marie de Magdala" says it plainly and is the shared French choice for John. A native reviewer may prefer the traditional form.

decisions.choice: la sœur de sa mère (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "sa sœur" after "sa mère" could mean Jesus's sister, so Balanced and Readable repeat "sa mère"; "sa tante" would be plain but adds a word John does not use.

decisions.choice: dada wa mama yake (B, R)
decisions.reason: In Swahili "dada yake" after "mama yake" could be read as Jesus's own sister, so Balanced and Readable keep the Greek's "his mother's sister" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "chị em gái"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese kinship words say whether a sister is older or younger ("dì" is usually a mother's younger sister). John does not say, so the neutral "chị em gái" is used.

decisions.choice: "이모" (B, R) for "his mother's sister"; "어머니의 자매" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean has a plain word for a mother's sister; Literal keeps the Greek phrase. "그리고" before the last name helps the reader count four women, as the meaning decision reads them.

decisions.choice: ቀለዮጳ for Clopas
alternatives: ቀሎጳ, a spelling made from the Greek
decisions.reason: The name keeps the form Amharic readers know from their Bible, as all names do.

decisions.choice: "Мария Клеопова" (L); "Мария, жена Клеопы" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The traditional Russian form of the name; Literal keeps the bare possessive of the Greek, Balanced and Readable say what it most likely means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "сестра его матери" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Russian "её сестра" after "его мать" would be clear, but Balanced and Readable keep the Greek's "his mother's sister" so the four women are counted as John counts them.

decisions.choice: "一方" (B); "母の姉妹"; "クロパの妻マリア"; "マグダラのマリア"
decisions.reason: The small word sets the women against the soldiers of the sentence before (m1 of 19:24); Balanced says 一方. 姉妹 leaves open whether she was older or younger, which Japanese 姉 or 妹 would decide. The list reads as four women (m1), joined by と and そして; "of Clopas" is most likely his wife (m2).

source.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ἰδὼν τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν παρεστῶτα ὃν ἠγάπα λέγει τῇ μητρί· Γύναι, ἴδε ὁ υἱός σου·

records.literal_gloss: Jesus then, having seen the mother and the disciple standing by whom he loved, says to the mother: Woman, behold the son of you.

en.L: So Jesus, seeing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and the disciple whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved standing by, says to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "Woman, look, your son."
en.B: Jesus saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother there, and near her the disciple whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved. He said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "Woman, look, here is your son."
en.R: Jesus saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother there. The disciple whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved was standing near her. Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "Mother, he is your son now."

es.L: Jesús, pues, viendo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre y al discípulo a quien amaba, que estaba al lado, dice a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Mujer, mira, tu hijo».
es.B: Jesús vio allí a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre, y junto a ella al discípulo a quien amaba. Le dijo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Mujer, mira, este es tu hijo».
es.R: Jesús vio allí a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre. El discípulo a quien Jesús amaba estaba cerca de ella. Entonces le dijo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Madre, desde ahora él es tu hijo».

fr.L: Jésus donc, voyant {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère et, se tenant près [d’elle], le disciple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait, dit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Femme, voici ton fils. »
fr.B: Jésus vit {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère, et près d’elle le disciple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait. Il dit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Femme, voici ton fils. »
fr.R: Jésus a vu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère. Le disciple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait se tenait près d’elle. Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Mère, c’est ton fils, maintenant. »

sw.L: Basi Yesu, alipomwona mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na yule mwanafunzi ambaye alimpenda akiwa amesimama karibu, anamwambia mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, "Mama, tazama, mwana wako."

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu, thấy mẹ và người môn đồ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu đứng bên cạnh, nói với mẹ: "Thưa bà, kìa, con của bà."

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thấy mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng đó. Người môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu đứng gần bà. Đức Giê-xu nói với mẹ: "Mẹ ơi, từ nay người này là con của mẹ."

ru.L: Иисус же, увидев мать и ученика, которого {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} любил, стоящего рядом, говорит матери: «Женщина, вот, твой сын.»
ru.B: Иисус увидел мать и рядом с ней ученика, которого {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} любил. Он сказал матери: «Женщина, вот твой сын.»
ru.R: Иисус увидел там свою мать. Рядом с ней стоял ученик, которого {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} любил. Иисус сказал матери: «Мама, теперь он твой сын.»

uk.L: Тож Ісус, побачивши матір і учня, якого {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} любив, що стояв поруч, каже матері: «Жінко, ось твій син.»
uk.B: Ісус побачив там свою матір, а біля неї учня, якого {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} любив. Він сказав матері: «Жінко, ось твій син.»

ja.L: それでイエスは、母と、愛しておられた弟子がそばに立っているのを見て、母に言われる。「婦人よ、見なさい、あなたの子だ。」
ja.B: イエスは、母とそのそばに立っている愛しておられた弟子とを見て、母に言われた。「婦人よ、ご覧なさい。この人があなたの子だ。」
ja.R: イエスは、そこに母がいるのを見られました。イエスが愛しておられた弟子も、そのそばに立っていました。イエスは母に言われました。「母さん、この人が今からあなたの息子だ。」

id.L: Ketika Yesus melihat ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} dan murid yang dikasihi-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} berdiri di dekatnya, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata kepada ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Perempuan, lihatlah, anakmu."
id.B: Yesus melihat ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} di situ, dan di dekatnya murid yang dikasihi-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Dia berkata kepada ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Ibu, lihatlah, inilah anak Ibu."
id.R: Yesus melihat ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} di situ. Murid yang dikasihi-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} berdiri di dekat ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Yesus berkata kepada ibu-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Ibu, sekarang dialah anak Ibu."

decisions.choice: Woman: a respectful address, as at Cana
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this address to his mother only twice, at Cana (2:4) and here. At Cana he said, "My hour has not yet come"; now his hour has come (12:23; 13:1; 17:1), and at the cross he speaks to her again in the same way. The address was courteous, not rude.

decisions.choice: look, your son: a declaration that makes a new bond, the disciple to be her son
alternatives: only pointing out the disciple standing there
decisions.reason: The words do not simply point at someone; they give the disciple to her as a son, and the next sentence gives her to him as a mother. The disciple acts on it at once (19:27).

decisions.choice: a dying son's care for his mother; perhaps also the start of a new family of his disciples
alternatives: chiefly a symbol, with the mother standing for a people of faith
decisions.reason: The first sense is plain: Jesus makes sure his mother will be cared for. His brothers did not yet believe in him (7:5). John may also mean more: from the cross Jesus joins his mother and his disciple as one family, and after the resurrection he calls his disciples "my brothers" (20:17). The text does not say so directly.

decisions.choice: the disciple whom Jesus loved: the disciple John does not name
decisions.reason: This disciple first appears at the last supper (13:23) and stands at the cross when the other disciples have scattered (16:32). The Gospel says he is the source of its witness (19:35; 21:24).

decisions.choice: said (B, R); says (L), and so through this passage (19:27, 19:28)
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English normally tells a story. This applies to every such verb in this passage.

decisions.choice: Woman
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "Woman" so that readers can connect this scene with Cana (2:4); the footnote on meaning decision m1 says the address was respectful. "Dear woman" would add warmth the word does not carry on its own.

decisions.choice: Mother, he is your son now (R)
decisions.reason: For young readers "Woman" sounds rude, which the Greek is not. She is his mother, so Readable uses the address a son would use, as it does at 2:4. "Now" shows that the words make a new bond (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Mujer (L, B); Madre (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the address is respectful (meaning decision m1), though "mujer" on its own can sound cold. Literal and Balanced keep it so that readers can link the cross with Cana; the footnote says it was courteous. Readable says "Madre", the address a son would use, and "desde ahora" shows that the words make a new bond (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: mira, tu hijo (L); mira, este es tu hijo (B)
decisions.reason: The word calls attention and gives the disciple to her as a son (meaning decision m2). "He ahí" is a familiar but dated form. Verse 27 uses the same wording for "tu madre". "Él" in Readable is the disciple and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Femme (L, B); Mère (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: Literal and Balanced keep "Femme" so that readers can connect the cross with Cana; the address was respectful (meaning decision m1). For young readers "Femme" sounds cold, so Readable uses the address a son would use, and "maintenant" shows that the words make a new bond (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Mama at every level
decisions.reason: The address is respectful in Greek (meaning decision m1). Calling a woman "Mwanamke!" to her face is rude in Swahili, so even Literal cannot keep the word without changing the tone. "Mama" is the respectful address to an older woman, and it also names her as his mother. It is the word used at Cana (2:4), so the link between the two scenes is kept.

decisions.choice: "Thưa bà" (L); "Thưa mẹ" (B); "Mẹ ơi" (R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide: Literal keeps the Greek "Woman" as a respectful "Thưa bà"; in Balanced and Readable a son speaking to his mother says "mẹ", since "bà" from a son would sound cold, which the Greek is not.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no past marker (L), "nói" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's historic present here and in 19:27-28 by leaving out "đã". "Nói" is the book's verb for Jesus speaking (docs/vietnamese-style.md).

decisions.choice: "여자여" (L); "어머니" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the Greek address is respectful, but "여자여" said to one's own mother sounds cold in Korean. Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable say "어머니". The English keeps "Woman" at Balanced, so the Korean differs there.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to his mother in the polite style (해요체: "보세요", "아들이에요"), and to the disciple in the plain style (19:27)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the plain style would be disrespectful from a son to his mother in Korean. Literal keeps "당신" for the Greek pronoun, as at 2:4.

decisions.choice: historic present "말씀하신다" (L); past (B, R), in 19:26-28
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past. One decision for 19:17-30.

decisions.choice: Mulher (L, B), Mãe (R), with "você" forms: o seu filho; a sua mãe (19:27)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to people with "você" (style section 4), his mother and the disciple included, so the possessive is "seu"; "teu" would bring in the archaic register of older Bibles. "Mulher" at Literal and Balanced keeps the link with Cana (2:4), as the English does; Readable says "Mãe".

decisions.choice: ሴት ሆይ (L, B); እናቴ (R)
alternatives: አንቺ ሴት, which sounds curt in Amharic
decisions.reason: "Woman" is respectful in Greek. Amharic ሴት ሆይ keeps the word with a formal vocative that is not cold, as in Matthew 15:28; Readable says "Mother", following the English and the book's choice for 2:4 and 19:26.

decisions.choice: ኢየሱስ ይወደው የነበረው ደቀ መዝሙር for the disciple whom Jesus loved
alternatives: የኢየሱስ ወዳጅ ደቀ መዝሙር (Jesus's beloved disciple)
decisions.reason: The phrase keeps John's relative clause and is used the same way each time the disciple appears, so readers can follow him through the book.

"Woman" is a respectful address in Greek (meaning decision m1; docs/john-terms.md). The address is worded exactly as at 2:4: Literal keeps the plain word, Balanced the dignified "नारी", which does not sound cold, and Readable says "माँ", since she is his mother, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "कहते हैं" (L); "कहा" (B, R), and likewise in 19:27-28
decisions.reason: John tells past events in the present tense here. Literal keeps the historic present, Balanced and Readable use the past (docs/john-terms.md); one decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "говорит" (L), here and in 19:27-28; "сказал" (B, R)
decisions.reason: John tells past events in the present (historic present). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past. One note for the passage.

decisions.choice: "Женщина" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the address so that readers can connect this scene with Cana (2:4); in Greek it is respectful, not cold (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "Мама" (R)
decisions.reason: Russian "Женщина!" said to one's mother sounds cold, which the Greek is not; she is his mother, so Readable uses the address a son would use, as the English Readable says "Mother".

decisions.choice: "Жінко" (L, B); "Мамо" (R)
decisions.reason: The convention settled for John: the address is respectful in Greek (meaning decision m1), and the Ukrainian vocative "Жінко" can be too; Readable says "Мамо", since she is his mother and a modern reader could hear "Жінко" as cold.

decisions.choice: "婦人よ" (L, B), "母さん" (R); "見なさい" (L), "ご覧なさい" (B)
decisions.reason: The address is respectful, as at Cana (m1), worded as in 2:4. Jesus keeps the plain style, but Balanced uses the gentler ご覧なさい to his mother. The words give the disciple to her as a son (m2), which Readable says with "今から".

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("言われる"); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells the crucifixion partly in the present. Literal keeps the Greek tense; Balanced and Readable narrate in the past. This holds through 19:17-30.

decisions.choice: "Perempuan" (L); "Ibu" (B, R), used also in place of "your" ("anak Ibu")
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: m1, a respectful address. Balanced and Readable say "Ibu", and Jesus says "anak Ibu" rather than "anakmu" to his mother, as an Indonesian son would.

es.R: Luego le dijo al discípulo: «Desde ahora ella es tu madre».

fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit au disciple : « Voici ta mère. »

sw.B: Kisha akamwambia yule mwanafunzi, "Tazama, huyu hapa ni mama yako."

vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người môn đồ: "Đây là mẹ của con."
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người môn đồ ấy: "Từ nay bà là mẹ của con."

pt.B: Depois disse ao discípulo: "Aqui está a sua mãe."
pt.R: Depois disse ao discípulo: "Agora ela é a sua mãe."

hi.L: फिर वे चेले से कहते हैं, "देखो, तुम्हारी माता।"
hi.B: फिर उन्होंने चेले से कहा, "देखो, यह तुम्हारी माता है।"

uk.R: Потім {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав учневі: «Тепер вона твоя мати.»

ja.L: それから弟子に言われる。「見なさい、あなたの母だ。」
ja.B: それから弟子に言われた。「ご覧なさい。この方があなたの母だ。」
ja.R: それから、弟子に言われました。「この方が、今からあなたの母だ。」

id.L: Kemudian {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata kepada murid itu, "Lihatlah, ibumu."
id.B: Kemudian {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata kepada murid itu, "Lihatlah, inilah ibumu."
id.R: Kemudian {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata kepada murid itu, "Sekarang dialah ibumu."

decisions.choice: look, your mother: the other half of the declaration in 19:26
decisions.reason: The two sayings match: she is to be his mother, and he is to be her son. Together they put her in the disciple's care as a son cares for his mother.

decisions.choice: She is your mother now (R)

decisions.choice: Desde ahora ella es tu madre (R)
decisions.reason: As in 19:26, Readable says what the words do: they give the disciple a mother to care for (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Jesus to the disciple: "con"
decisions.reason: As the style guide: Jesus speaks to a disciple as "con". It also suits the new family bond he is making.

pt.R: Daquele momento em diante, o discípulo levou a mãe de Jesus para morar na casa dele.

am.L: ከዚያችም ሰዓት ጀምሮ ደቀ መዝሙሩ ወደ ራሱ [ቤት] ወሰዳት።
am.B: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ደቀ መዝሙሩ ወደ ቤቱ ወሰዳት።
am.R: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ያ ደቀ መዝሙር በቤቱ እንድትኖር ወሰዳት።

ru.B: С того времени ученик взял её к себе в дом.

ja.R: その時から、その弟子は、イエスの母を自分の家に迎えて、いっしょに暮らしました。

id.B: Sejak saat itu murid itu menerima dia di rumahnya sendiri.
id.R: Sejak saat itu, murid itu membawa dia untuk tinggal di rumahnya.

decisions.choice: from that hour: from that time on, starting then
alternatives: from Jesus's appointed hour, meaning the cross as the hour of his glory
decisions.reason: Here "hour" means a time of day: the disciple acted at once. But John has spoken of Jesus's hour throughout the Gospel (2:4; 12:23; 13:1; 17:1), and at the cross that hour has come, so the word may also remind readers of it.

decisions.choice: into his own: into his own home, as one of his household
alternatives: into his own care, without saying where she lived
decisions.reason: "His own" is a common way of saying "his home" or "his own people" (1:11; 16:32). Taking her into it means more than a place to stay: she became part of his household.

decisions.choice: From that time on (B); From then on (R); from that hour (L)
decisions.reason: Here "hour" is a time of day, not Jesus's appointed hour (which Balanced writes as "hour"), so Balanced and Readable say "time". Literal keeps "hour" so that the possible echo can be seen (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: desde entonces (B); a partir de ese momento (R); desde aquella hora (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: here "hora" is a time of day, not Jesus's appointed hour, so Balanced and Readable do not say "hora"; Literal keeps it so that the possible echo can be seen (meaning decision m1). "Acoger" and "llevar a vivir" show that she became part of his household (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: dès cette heure-là (L); à partir de ce moment (B); dès ce moment-là (R); chez lui
decisions.reason: Here "hour" is a time of day, not Jesus's appointed hour, so Balanced and Readable say "moment"; Literal keeps "heure" so that the possible echo can be seen (meaning decision m1). French "chez lui" says "into his own home" without a supplied word (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: alimchukua kwake (L), with no bracket
decisions.reason: "Kwake" (to his place, to his own) says what the Greek idiom says, so Literal needs no supplied word where the English brackets "[home]". Balanced and Readable say "nyumbani kwake" (into his home). Literal keeps "saa" (hour) for the possible echo of Jesus's hour (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "उन्हें" (honorific) for Jesus's mother
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks of Jesus's mother with the honorific, as the women at the cross take honorific agreement (खड़ी थीं) and as Hindi does for an elder mother.

decisions.choice: "с того времени" (B); "с тех пор" (R)
decisions.reason: Here "hour" is a time of day, not Jesus's appointed hour (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable do not say "час"; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: "その時から" at every level
decisions.reason: Here hour means a time of day: the disciple acted at once (m1). Writing 時 in kanji keeps the word of Jesus's hour (2:4; 12:23; 13:1) in view, as the Greek may intend.

source.text: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤδη πάντα τετέλεσται ἵνα τελειωθῇ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Διψῶ.

records.literal_gloss: After this, knowing the Jesus that already all things have been finished, so that might be completed the Scripture, says: I thirst.

en.L: After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had now been finished, so that the Scripture might be completed, says, "I thirst."
en.B: After this, Jesus knew that everything had now been finished. So that the Scripture would be completed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I am thirsty."
en.R: After this, Jesus knew that everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come to do was now finished. To make the Scripture come fully true, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I am thirsty."

es.L: Después de esto, sabiendo Jesús que ya todo había sido terminado, para que se llevara a término la Escritura, dice: «Tengo sed».
es.B: Después de esto, Jesús sabía que ya todo estaba terminado. Para que la Escritura se cumpliera por completo, dijo: «Tengo sed».
es.R: Después de esto, Jesús sabía que ya había terminado todo lo que había venido a hacer. Para que se cumpliera por completo lo que dice la Escritura, dijo: «Tengo sed».

fr.L: Après cela, Jésus, sachant que déjà tout était achevé, afin que l’Écriture s’accomplisse pleinement, dit : « J’ai soif. »
fr.B: Après cela, Jésus savait que tout était désormais achevé. Pour que l’Écriture s’accomplisse pleinement, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « J’ai soif. »
fr.R: Après cela, Jésus savait que tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était venu faire était maintenant achevé. Pour que l’Écriture se réalise complètement, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « J’ai soif. »

sw.L: Baada ya hayo, Yesu, akijua kwamba sasa yote yamekwisha, ili Maandiko yakamilike, anasema, "Nina kiu."
sw.B: Baada ya hayo, Yesu alijua kwamba sasa yote yamekwisha. Ili Maandiko yakamilike, akasema, "Nina kiu."
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Yesu alijua kwamba kila kitu alichokuja kufanya sasa kimekwisha. Ili Maandiko yatimie kikamilifu, akasema, "Nina kiu."

vi.L: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu, biết rằng mọi sự nay đã được hoàn tất, để Kinh Thánh được trọn vẹn, nói: "Ta khát."
vi.B: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu biết rằng mọi việc nay đã hoàn tất. Để lời Kinh Thánh được trọn vẹn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Ta khát."
vi.R: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu biết rằng mọi việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến để làm nay đã xong. Để lời Kinh Thánh được trọn vẹn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Ta khát nước."

ko.L: 이 일 후에, 예수께서는 이미 모든 것이 다 이루어졌음을 아시고, 성경을 온전히 이루시려고 말씀하신다. "목마르다."
ko.B: 그 뒤에 예수께서는 이제 모든 일이 다 이루어진 것을 아셨다. 그리고 성경 말씀을 온전히 이루시려고 말씀하셨다. "목이 마르다."
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서는 이 세상에서 하실 일을 이제 모두 마치신 것을 아셨다. 그리고 성경 말씀이 온전히 이루어지게 하시려고 말씀하셨다. "목이 마르다."

pt.L: Depois disso, Jesus, sabendo que todas as coisas já estavam consumadas, para que se completasse a Escritura, diz: "Tenho sede."
pt.B: Depois disso, Jesus sabia que tudo já estava consumado. Para que a Escritura se cumprisse plenamente, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Tenho sede."
pt.R: Depois disso, Jesus sabia que tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha vindo fazer já estava consumado. Para que a Escritura se cumprisse por completo, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Tenho sede."

am.L: ከዚህ በኋላ ኢየሱስ ሁሉ ነገር አሁን እንደ ተፈጸመ አውቆ፣ መጽሐፍ ፍጻሜውን ያገኝ ዘንድ፦ «ተጠማሁ» ይላል።
am.B: ከዚህ በኋላ ኢየሱስ ሁሉ ነገር አሁን እንደ ተፈጸመ አወቀ። የመጽሐፍ ቃል ፍጻሜውን እንዲያገኝም፦ «ተጠምቻለሁ» አለ።
am.R: ከዚህ በኋላ ኢየሱስ ሊሠራው የመጣው ሥራ ሁሉ አሁን እንደ ተፈጸመ አወቀ። በመጻሕፍት የተጻፈው ቃል ሙሉ በሙሉ እውን እንዲሆን፦ «ተጠምቻለሁ» አለ።

hi.L: इसके बाद यीशु, यह जानकर कि अब सब कुछ पूरा हो चुका है, ताकि पवित्रशास्त्र पूरा हो, कहते हैं, "मैं प्यासा हूँ।"
hi.B: इसके बाद यीशु ने जाना कि अब सब कुछ पूरा हो चुका है। तब पवित्रशास्त्र पूरा होने के लिए उन्होंने कहा, "मैं प्यासा हूँ।"

ru.L: После этого Иисус, зная, что всё уже совершилось, чтобы исполнилось до конца Писание, говорит: «Жажду.»
ru.B: После этого Иисус, зная, что всё уже совершилось, сказал, чтобы до конца исполнилось Писание: «Хочу пить.»
ru.R: После этого Иисус понял, что всё, ради чего {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} пришёл, уже совершилось. И чтобы Писание исполнилось полностью, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сказал: «Хочу пить.»

uk.L: Після цього Ісус, знаючи, що все вже звершено, щоб довершилося Писання, каже: «Прагну.»
uk.B: Після цього Ісус знав, що все вже звершено. І щоб довершилося Писання, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав: «Я спраглий.»
uk.R: Після цього Ісус знав, що все, для чого {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} прийшов, уже звершено. Щоб Писання збулося до кінця, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав: «Я хочу пити.»

ja.L: この後、イエスは、すでにすべてのことが完了したことを知って、聖書が全うされるために、言われる。「渇く。」
ja.B: この後、イエスは、すべてのことが今や成し遂げられたのを知って、聖書が全うされるために、「渇く」と言われた。
ja.R: その後、イエスは、ご自分がするために来たことが、もう全部終わったことを知っておられました。そして、聖書に書いてあることが残らず本当になるように、「のどが渇いた」と言われました。

id.L: Sesudah itu, karena Yesus tahu bahwa segala sesuatu telah selesai, supaya genaplah Kitab Suci, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata, "Aku haus."
id.B: Sesudah itu, Yesus tahu bahwa segala sesuatu sudah selesai. Supaya genaplah Kitab Suci, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata, "Aku haus."
id.R: Sesudah itu, Yesus tahu bahwa semua yang harus {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} lakukan sudah selesai. Supaya apa yang dikatakan Kitab Suci benar-benar terjadi, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata, "Aku haus."

decisions.choice: so that the Scripture might be completed goes with "he says": he said "I thirst" to fulfill the Scripture
alternatives: it goes with "all things had been finished": everything was done so that the Scripture would be completed
decisions.reason: The purpose clause stands between the two verbs and could belong to either. Joined to "he says", it explains the saying by the Scripture about thirst (meaning decision m3), as 19:24 and 19:36 explain other details. Joined to "finished", it would say that the whole work was done to complete the Scripture, and "I thirst" would be simply his need. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: finished ... completed: the work the Father gave Jesus is done; the Scripture is brought to completion
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one Jesus says in 19:30, "It is finished". The second is not John's usual word for fulfilling Scripture (19:24) but the word Jesus used for completing the Father's work (4:34; 5:36; 17:4). John uses it to show that the Scripture, like the work, has reached its goal.

decisions.choice: I thirst: Psalm 69:22, with Psalm 22:16 in the background
alternatives: only a statement of physical thirst, with no Scripture in mind
decisions.reason: Psalm 69:22 says "for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink", and the next verse in John has the sour wine. Psalm 22, already quoted in 19:24, says "my tongue sticks to my jaws" (22:16). Both psalms are prayers of the righteous sufferer. The thirst was real: he had been flogged and had hung on the cross for hours.

decisions.choice: knowing: Jesus goes to his death aware and in control
decisions.reason: John often says what Jesus knew at turning points of the passion (13:1, 3; 18:4). He lays down his life of his own accord (10:18), and he speaks this word knowing that his work is now done.

decisions.choice: finished (as in 19:30); completed (as in 17:4); I thirst (L); I am thirsty (B, R)
alternatives: I am thirsty at every level
decisions.reason: "Finished" is the same English word as Jesus's last saying (19:30), and "completed" the same as "having completed the work" in 17:4, so the links in the Greek stay visible (meaning decision m2). Readable says what had been finished, from 17:4.

decisions.choice: terminado (as "Está terminado" in 19:30); se llevara a término (L); se cumpliera por completo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one Jesus says in 19:30, so every level uses "terminar" in both places (meaning decision m2). The second is not John's usual verb for fulfilling Scripture: Literal shows it with "llevar a término", the phrase Balanced uses for completing the Father's works at 5:36; Balanced and Readable say that the Scripture was fulfilled completely. Readable says what had been finished, from 17:4.

decisions.choice: achevé (as "C'est achevé" in 19:30); s'accomplisse pleinement (L, B); se réalise complètement (R)
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one of Jesus's last word in 19:30, so both are "achever" and the link stays visible (meaning decision m2). The second is not John's usual verb for fulfilling Scripture ("s'accomplir", 19:24), so French adds "pleinement" to show that the Scripture is brought to completion. "J'ai soif" serves every level.

decisions.choice: yamekwisha (finished), as "Imekwisha" in 19:30; yakamilike (completed), as "kuikamilisha kazi" in 4:34
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one of Jesus's last word (19:30), so Swahili uses the same verb "-isha"; the second is the verb for completing the Father's work (meaning decision m2), so it is "-kamilika", not "-timia", which 19:24 uses for fulfilling Scripture. The links stay visible, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "다 이루어졌다" for tetelestai (here and 19:30); "온전히 이루다" for the Scripture being completed
decisions.reason: John uses the same verb here and in Jesus's last word (19:30); Korean keeps one phrase for both. The passive "이루어졌다" follows the Greek and avoids the wording of older versions.

decisions.choice: consumado (as in 19:30); Tenho sede (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Jesus says in 19:30, so Portuguese uses "consumado" in both places, as the English keeps "finished" (meaning decision m2). Portuguese says thirst with "Tenho sede" at every level; it has no shorter, more literal form to keep at Literal.

decisions.choice: እንደ ተፈጸመ (finished, as in 19:30); ፍጻሜውን ያገኝ (L, B), ሙሉ በሙሉ እውን እንዲሆን (R) for the Scripture being completed
alternatives: ተጠናቀቀ (completed), which sounds like a task ticked off
ይፈጸም for the Scripture, the word kept for "fulfil" in 19:24 and 19:36
decisions.reason: Amharic ፈጸመ means both to carry through and to fulfil, which suits John's word for the finished work. The Scripture's completion, a different Greek word, is said with ፍጻሜ (its goal reached), so it stays apart from the plain "fulfilled" of 19:24 and 19:36.

decisions.choice: "पूरा हो चुका है" for finished; "पूरा हो" for completed
decisions.reason: John uses two related verbs, one for the finished work and one for Scripture brought to completion (meaning decision m2). Hindi says both with "पूरा होना", which also carries the "It is finished" of 19:30 ("पूरा हुआ") and the completed work of 17:4.

decisions.choice: "совершилось" (as "Совершилось" in 19:30)
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one of Jesus's last word in 19:30, so every level uses "совершиться" in both places (meaning decision m2); "исполнилось до конца" gives the second verb, the completing of Scripture.

decisions.choice: "Жажду" (L); "Хочу пить" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the one-word Greek in the bookish Russian verb; Balanced and Readable say it in everyday Russian.

decisions.choice: "完了した" (L), "成し遂げられた" (B), "終わった" (R), as in 19:30; "全うされる" (L, B)
alternatives: "成就する" for the second verb
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one Jesus says in 19:30, so each level uses the same word in both places. The second is not John's usual word for fulfilling Scripture but the word for completing the Father's work (m2); 全うされる keeps it apart from the 成就する of 19:24.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause placed before "言われる"
decisions.reason: The purpose clause goes with the saying (m1); Japanese puts it directly before the verb of saying, so it cannot be read with "knowing".

records.literal_gloss: A vessel was lying of sour wine full; a sponge then full of the sour wine on hyssop having put around, they brought [it] to him the mouth.

en.L: A jar full of sour wine was standing [there]; so, putting a sponge full of the sour wine on hyssop, they brought [it] to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.B: A jar full of sour wine stood there. So they put a sponge soaked in the sour wine on a stalk of hyssop and raised it to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lips.
en.R: A jar of sour wine was sitting nearby. So they soaked a sponge in it, put the sponge on the end of a hyssop stick, and lifted it up to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.

es.L: Estaba [allí] una vasija llena de vino agrio; poniendo, pues, en un hisopo una esponja llena del vino agrio, [la] acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca.
es.B: Había allí una vasija llena de vino agrio. Así que empaparon una esponja en el vino agrio, la pusieron en una rama de hisopo y {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} la acercaron a los labios.
es.R: Cerca de allí había una jarra de vino agrio. Así que mojaron una esponja en el vino, la pusieron en la punta de una vara de hisopo y {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} la acercaron a la boca.

fr.L: Un vase plein de vin aigre se trouvait [là] ; ayant donc fixé sur de l’hysope une éponge pleine du vin aigre, ils [la] portèrent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche.
fr.B: Il y avait là une jarre pleine de vin aigre. Ils fixèrent donc au bout d’une tige d’hysope une éponge imbibée de ce vin aigre, et l’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} lèvres.
fr.R: Il y avait près de là une jarre de vin aigre. Ils y ont trempé une éponge, ils l’ont mise au bout d’une tige d’hysope, et ils l’ont levée jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche.

sw.L: Mtungi uliojaa divai chungu ulikuwa umewekwa [pale]; basi, wakiweka sifongo iliyojaa divai chungu juu ya hisopo, wakaipeleka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.

sw.R: Karibu pale palikuwa na mtungi wa divai chungu. Basi wakachovya sifongo ndani yake, wakaiweka sifongo kwenye ncha ya fimbo ya hisopo, wakaiinua mpaka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.

vi.L: Có một cái bình đầy rượu chua để [ở đó]; vậy họ đặt một miếng bọt biển thấm đầy rượu chua trên kinh giới mà đưa lên miệng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

vi.R: Gần đó có một cái bình đựng rượu chua. Họ nhúng một miếng bọt biển vào rượu, gắn nó vào đầu một cây kinh giới, rồi đưa lên miệng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 신 포도주가 가득 담긴 그릇이 [거기] 놓여 있었다. 그래서 그들은 신 포도주를 가득 적신 해면을 우슬초에 매달아 그분의 입에 갖다 대었다.
ko.B: 거기에 신 포도주가 가득 담긴 항아리가 있었다. 그래서 그들은 해면을 신 포도주에 적셔 우슬초 줄기에 매달아 예수의 입에 갖다 대었다.
ko.R: 가까이에 신 포도주가 든 항아리가 있었다. 그래서 그들은 스펀지를 신 포도주에 적셨다. 그리고 그것을 우슬초 막대 끝에 꽂아 예수의 입에 갖다 대었다.

pt.L: Havia ali um vaso cheio de vinho azedo; então, pondo uma esponja cheia do vinho azedo num hissopo, [a] levaram à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca.

ru.L: Стоял [там] сосуд, полный кислого вина; [воины,] наполнив губку кислым вином и наложив на иссоп, поднесли к {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} устам.
ru.B: Там стоял кувшин с кислым вином. Солдаты пропитали губку кислым вином, насадили её на стебель иссопа и поднесли к {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} губам.
ru.R: Рядом стоял кувшин с кислым вином. Солдаты намочили в нём губку, надели губку на конец палочки иссопа и поднесли ко рту Иисуса.

uk.L: Стояла посудина, повна оцту; тож, наклавши на ісоп губку, повну оцту, піднесли [її] до {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} уст.
uk.B: Там стояла посудина, повна кислого вина. Тож вони наклали губку, намочену в кислому вині, на стебло ісопу й піднесли до {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} уст.
uk.R: Неподалік стояла посудина з кислим вином. Тож вони намочили в ньому губку, настромили її на гілку ісопу й піднесли до {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} рота.

ja.L: 酸いぶどう酒の満ちた器が置いてあった。それで彼らは、酸いぶどう酒を含ませた海綿をヒソプに付けて、イエスの口もとに差し出した。
ja.B: そこには、酸いぶどう酒を満たした器が置いてあった。そこで彼らは、酸いぶどう酒をたっぷり含ませた海綿をヒソプの茎に付けて、イエスの口に差し出した。
ja.R: すぐ近くに、すっぱくなったぶどう酒の入ったつぼが置いてありました。そこで彼らは、スポンジをそのぶどう酒にひたし、ヒソプの枝の先に付けて、イエスの口もとまで持ち上げました。

id.L: Di situ ada sebuah bejana penuh anggur asam; lalu mereka mencucukkan bunga karang yang penuh anggur asam pada sebatang hisop dan mendekatkannya ke mulut-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.
id.B: Di situ ada sebuah tempayan penuh anggur asam. Lalu mereka mencelupkan bunga karang ke dalam anggur asam itu, menaruhnya pada sebatang hisop, dan mengangkatnya ke bibir-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.
id.R: Di dekat situ ada sebuah tempayan berisi anggur asam. Jadi mereka mencelupkan bunga karang ke dalamnya, menaruh bunga karang itu di ujung sebatang ranting hisop, lalu mengangkatnya ke mulut-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.

decisions.choice: sour wine: cheap wine gone sour, the everyday drink of soldiers and laborers
alternatives: drugged wine offered to dull pain
decisions.reason: The word means wine that has turned sour, which mixed with water was a common drink for soldiers and workers. It is the word in the Greek of Psalm 69:22 (see 19:28). Giving it may have been simple relief rather than mockery; John does not say. It is not the wine mixed with myrrh that Mark says Jesus refused before he was crucified (Mark 15:23).

decisions.choice: hyssop: the plant used to put the blood of the Passover lamb on the doorposts
alternatives: only the nearest plant stem, with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Hyssop is a small, bushy plant. Israel used a bunch of it to put the blood of the Passover lamb on the doorframes (Exodus 12:22), and it was used in cleansing (Leviticus 14:4; Psalm 51:9). John has told the story so that Jesus dies on the day the Passover lambs are killed (18:28; 19:14) and calls him the Lamb of God (1:29); he applies a Passover rule to him in 19:36. The mention of hyssop most likely points to this.

decisions.choice: on hyssop (all manuscripts)
alternatives: on a javelin: a guess, found in one late manuscript, that a similar word for the Roman javelin (in Latin, pilum) stood here
decisions.reason: A stalk of hyssop seems too weak to lift a soaked sponge, so it has been suggested that John wrote a very similar word meaning "javelin", and that a copyist misread it. The guess appears in only one late manuscript, of about the eleventh century; all the early manuscripts read "hyssop". A small branch would be enough, since a cross was often not much higher than a man. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they: the people standing by the cross, most likely the soldiers
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. The soldiers are the last group said to act (19:23-24), and sour wine was their drink, so they are the most likely ones.

decisions.choice: jar; sour wine; hyssop (L); a stalk of hyssop (B); a hyssop stick (R)
decisions.reason: "Vinegar" today means something no one drinks; "sour wine" says what it was (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say what part of the plant was used. Every level keeps "hyssop" so the Passover link can be seen (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: vasija (L, B); jarra (R); vino agrio; hisopo (L); una rama de hisopo (B); una vara de hisopo (R)
decisions.reason: "Vinagre" today means something no one drinks; "vino agrio" says what it was (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say what part of the plant was used, and every level keeps "hisopo" so that the Passover link can be seen (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: vin aigre; hysope (L); une tige d'hysope (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Vinaigre" today means something no one drinks; "vin aigre" says what it was, the soldiers' everyday drink (meaning decision m1). Every level keeps "hysope" so that the Passover link can be seen (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say which part of the plant was used.

decisions.choice: divai chungu (sour wine); hisopo at every level
decisions.reason: "Siki" (vinegar) is something no one drinks; the word means cheap wine gone sour, the drink of soldiers (meaning decision m1), so every level says "divai chungu". Every level keeps "hisopo" so the link with the Passover can be seen (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say what part of the plant was used.

decisions.choice: "kinh giới" for hyssop
decisions.reason: "kinh giới" is the name Vietnamese Bibles have given the hyssop of Exodus 12:22, and keeping it keeps the Passover link the meaning decision notes. The Vietnamese herb of that name is not the same plant, so a reviewer should confirm the term.

decisions.choice: "rượu chua"
decisions.reason: "giấm" today means cooking vinegar; "rượu chua" is soured wine, the cheap drink the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "신 포도주"; "우슬초" (L); "우슬초 줄기" (B); "우슬초 막대" (R)

decisions.choice: It is finished: the work is completed, carried through to its goal, and it stands
alternatives: it is over: his life has ended
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something to its end or goal. It is the word of 19:28, and it answers Jesus's words about completing the work the Father gave him (4:34; 17:4) and loving his own "to the end" (13:1). The tense means a thing done whose result remains. It is a cry of completion, not of defeat.

decisions.choice: handed over his spirit: he died, giving up his life himself
alternatives: breathed his last, with nothing more meant
decisions.reason: "To give up the spirit" is a way of saying someone died, and "spirit" here is his own life and breath, as in Luke 23:46. John's verb is the one used all through the passion for handing someone over (Judas, 18:2, 5; the chief priests, 18:30, 35; Pilate, 19:16). Now Jesus hands over his own life: no one takes it from him (10:18).

decisions.choice: his own spirit; John may also hint that the Spirit is now to be given
alternatives: a plain statement that he died, with no reference to the Holy Spirit
he handed over the Holy Spirit to those at the cross
decisions.reason: John said the Spirit would be given once Jesus was glorified (7:39), and the risen Jesus breathes on the disciples and gives them the Holy Spirit (20:22). Some read a hint of that here, since the words could also mean "handed over the Spirit". But the phrase is a natural way to describe death, and the Spirit is given in 20:22. The sense "his own spirit" is certain; a further hint is possible but not clear.

decisions.choice: bowing his head: first he bowed his head, then he died
decisions.reason: The order of the words shows the order of events: Jesus bows his head and then hands over his spirit, as one who chooses the moment.

decisions.choice: It is finished (every level); handed over his spirit, with "spirit" in lowercase
decisions.reason: "Finished" is the word used in 19:28, so the link stays visible. "Handed over" keeps the verb John uses throughout the passion (meaning decision m2). "Spirit" is lowercase because it is his own spirit (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: and died (R)
decisions.reason: Young readers may not know that "handed over his spirit" means that he died, so Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: Está terminado (every level); entregó el / su espíritu, lowercase
decisions.reason: "Está terminado" uses the verb of 19:28, so the link stays visible, and says that the work is complete and stands (meaning decision m1); the traditional "Consumado es" is no longer everyday Spanish. "Entregar" keeps the verb used throughout the passion for handing someone over (meaning decision m2), and "espíritu" is lowercase because it is his own spirit (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: y murió (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: young readers may not know that "entregó su espíritu" means that he died, so Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: C'est achevé (every level); livra son esprit, with "esprit" in lowercase
decisions.reason: "C'est achevé" says a work carried through to its end, and uses the verb of 19:28 (meaning decision m1); the familiar "Tout est accompli" adds "tout" and blurs the link with "accomplir" for Scripture. "Livrer" keeps the verb used all through the passion for handing over (meaning decision m2), where "rendre l'esprit" would be only an idiom for dying. "Esprit" is lowercase because it is his own spirit (meaning decision m3). Readable adds "il est mort", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Imekwisha; akaikabidhi roho yake, with "roho" in lowercase
decisions.reason: "Kukata roho" is the everyday idiom for dying, but John's verb is the one used all through the passion for handing Jesus over (meaning decision m2), which this passage renders "kukabidhi" (19:11, 16). So Jesus "hands over" his own spirit, a phrase Swahili readers also know from Luke 23:46. "Roho" is lowercase because it is his own spirit (meaning decision m3). Readable adds "akafa" (and died), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "trao thần linh", lowercase
decisions.reason: "trút linh hồn" is the familiar idiom for dying but speaks of the soul and of letting go. "trao" keeps the Greek "handed over" (he gives up his life himself), and lowercase "thần linh" keeps "spirit" as the style guide does where it is not the Holy Spirit, leaving room for the hint the meaning decision notes.

decisions.choice: "영을 넘겨주셨다" at every level; Readable adds "숨을 거두셨다"
decisions.reason: "넘겨주다" is the verb used for each hand-over of Jesus in the trial; John uses it here for Jesus giving up his own life. "영", not "성령", because the meaning decision reads his own spirit and leaves the hint of the Spirit to a footnote.

decisions.choice: Está consumado, at every level
decisions.reason: "Consumar" means to bring something to its end and goal, which is the sense of the verb (meaning decision m1), and it ties the saying to verse 28. "Está terminado" or "Acabou" would sound like mere stopping. The phrase is short and common, and every level keeps it, as the English keeps "It is finished".

decisions.choice: «ተፈጸመ» (It is finished) at every level
decisions.reason: ተፈጸመ says that the work has been carried through to its goal, the sense the meaning decision gives; አበቃ would say only that it has stopped.

decisions.choice: "आत्मा सौंप दी"
decisions.reason: "Handed over his spirit" means he died, giving up his life himself (meaning decision m2). "सौंप देना" keeps the verb of handing over that runs through the passion story; Readable adds that he died, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Совершилось" at every level
decisions.reason: The verb of 19:28, so the link stays; it says a work carried through to its goal (meaning decision m1). "Совершилось" is the modern form of the familiar word.

decisions.choice: "предал дух" (L); "отдал свой дух" (B, R), with "дух" in lowercase
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "предать", the verb of handing over that runs through the passion; Balanced and Readable say "отдал", since the idiom "испустить дух" hides that he gives up his life himself (meaning decision m2). Readable adds "и умер", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Звершено" (L, B); "Усе звершено" (R), the same verb as "звершено" in verse 28
decisions.reason: "Звершити" is to carry a work through to its goal (meaning decision m1), not merely to end; using it in verses 28 and 30 keeps John's link between them. "Дух" stays lowercase: his own spirit.

decisions.choice: "完了した" (L); "成し遂げられた" (B); "すべて終わった" (R)
decisions.reason: The work is completed and carried through to its goal, and it stands (m1). Literal says it with the plain word for something completed; Balanced says it was accomplished; Readable uses the everyday word, with すべて so that it is not heard as "I am finished".

decisions.choice: "霊を引き渡された" (L), "霊をお渡しになった" (B, R); "息を引き取られました" (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means that he died, giving up his life himself (m2), with the verb used all through the passion for handing over. Literal and Balanced keep the verb and the word 霊, which also leaves room for the hint in m3; Readable adds that he died, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Telah selesai" (L); "Sudah selesai" (B, R)
decisions.reason: m1: the work is completed, carried through to its goal; the same root as "menyelesaikan" in 17:4, as the Greek links them. "Sudah selesai" is the only natural Indonesian for it.
